items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And he asked Buddy -- Buddy, I think he was about 18 at the time -- if he thinks he could put a number together for Irene Delroy, which he did. ... And he taught her this little number

ctx.x: Billy Pierce gave Buddy his first opportunity to teach. He had this idea of so many of the white performers needing this sort of rhythm dancing, and he gave Buddy his first opportunity with -- somebody, Irene Delroy -- she was in a show, in the Greenwich Village Follies, something like that. I hope I'm right.

And he asked Buddy -- Buddy, I think he was about 18 at the time -- if he thinks he could put a number together for Irene Delroy, which he did. He'd never done it before, but he just had this gift of making a girl look very cute with taps, without looking sort of hefty or awkward. And he taught her this little number, and she went back into the show, stopped the show, and that's what caused the influx of white show biz peoples at that time going to the Billy Pierce Studios and everybody wanting these hit numbers…
